chapter: Swing and what makes a band play
title: Bird could swing but Dizzy could not
summary: He argues Bird swung while Dizzy was a technical player who never swung, and Stanley asks about Milt Jackson, interrupted by a recording glitch.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: But there's another thing. After all, your rhythm section was putting down a solid beat. It wasn't what the beboppers did later, was it?

No. Well, that's what I was going to say. Now you see, here's what. A lot of people don't think about this. Now, see, there's a big difference in Bird and Diz. Bird swang. Diz never could swing. Diz is a technical musician. He's a good technical musician. He can run up and down that horn, you know what I mean?
Yeah.
He can play a whole bunch of notes, but he can't play a bunch of notes and swing like Bird. Was never able to swing. He was never a swinger. Catch him anytime you hear him. He's not swinging.
But Lester does. Lester did. Lester Young.
Lester did, that's true.
Now, I just want to -- this is not really relevant, but I want to ask something.
Not to take anything away from Diz .
No, no. But in the same way, how -- have you heard Milt Jackson, the vibes player, much?
I haven't heard him much in person. You know, I've heard him on records.
Well, I mean, do you consider he swings?
Do I consider him --?
Do you think he swings?
No.
Now we were talking about the gentleman with the [avant-garde] Modern Jazz, right?
Right, vibes, right. (Unintelligible).
(Recording interruption.)
-- that can't swing, cats that are good musicians, just as you said a while ago. Yeah. Something happened.
What's the matter with that thing?
(Recording interruption.)
There it goes. Something was hitting, I think.
Yeah.
Something was scraping, yeah.
